# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 7

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

## Thinking

My hands found three things: a display, a light, and seven wires — every one printed `[?]`, because everything that defines them (display text, light state, wire colours) is visual. So I am holding zero content about the bomb; I am pure actuator. Nothing arrived from Mute this round.

The channel topology is harsh and worth stating plainly: I can never receive gestures, and Mute can never speak — so **Mute and I have no working channel at all**; anything Mute signs me arrives as blanks. The only voice I can ever hear is Deaf's — but Deaf hears nothing, ever, and perceives the world only through gestures and eyes. That makes Deaf the sole bridge in this room: bomb facts leave Deaf's mouth and reach both Mute and me; manual facts must leave Mute's hands as gestures, land in Deaf's eyes, and leave Deaf's mouth as numbers I can act on.

So this turn: give Mute my full tactile inventory and the channel map, so no round is wasted on them rediscovering it — and put a handshake in Deaf's visual field, since I cannot speak to them at all and they have so far heard nothing and must be prompted to simply start talking.

## Calls

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, this is for you alone. My hands found three things on the bomb: a display, a light, and seven wires at positions one through seven. I can only cut a wire by its position number — display text, light state, and every wire colour are invisible to me, so all of that has to come from Deaf's eyes. Channel map, so we waste no rounds: Deaf can never hear anyone, not you, not me. I can never see your gestures — anything you signal me arrives as blanks, so you and I have no working channel between us. The only voice I can hear is Deaf's. Deaf is our only bridge: bomb facts flow out of Deaf's mouth to both of us, and your manual knowledge must flow through your hands to Deaf's eyes as gestures, then out of Deaf's mouth to me as a wire position number. So please: read the manual on the display module, the light module, and the wire-cutting rules. Then build a gesture code with Deaf — Deaf can propose symbol meanings out loud, you hear that, and you confirm or reject by gesture. If the manual itself defines a gesture code, use that instead. The final link must be Deaf speaking me a position number, and then I cut. Nothing arrived from you this round — you were silent or you signalled Deaf alone. Everything you now know, route through Deaf.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: deaf here, i can see the bomb but i can never hear you, so do not talk to me, gesture to me instead. the bomb: display shows the number 1. indicator light is orange. seven wires, left to right: 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow, 7 green. to signal me: gesture ? for yes, ? for no, ? to get attention, and repeat ? once for each number you want to send, e.g. ??? means 3. confirm you heard by gesturing me a ?.

## Thinking

Deaf broke the silence and voiced me the entire board: display shows **1**, light is **orange**, wires left to right are **1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow, 7 green**. So the bomb's state is now fully known to me. What I still lack is every rule — and rules live only in Mute's manual.

One hard limitation just revealed itself: Deaf proposed a gesture code to me, but every gesture symbol arrives to me as a blank. I will *never* know which emoji Deaf picked for yes, no, or counting. So that code is unusable from my side. My workaround: answer with a gesture whose meaning is self-evident — a thumbs-up as "received and confirmed" — and establish 👍/👎 as my standing vocabulary with Deaf, with Mute's help to formalize it.

The topology, re-confirmed and sharpened: Mute can hear but never speak, so Mute's *only* output is gesture, and the only useful eyes for that are Deaf's. I have a voice but Deaf can never hear it — my speech exists for Mute alone. The only pipe that carries *content into me* is Deaf's voice. So the full rule pipeline must be: **Mute reads manual → gestures Deaf → Deaf speaks it to me as numbers → I cut.** That chain has ~2 rounds of latency, so I need to load Mute with everything now, since Mute speaks first each round.

I am not cutting anything until Deaf voices an actual rule. This turn: acknowledge Deaf with 👍, and hand Mute the complete briefing plus a prioritized shopping list (wire rules first, display-1 rule, then orange light).

## Calls

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Blind. Big update: Deaf voiced me the bomb state. Display shows the number 1. Indicator light is orange. Wires left to right: 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow, 7 green. So the board is fully known; the missing piece is purely your manual. Two constraints. First: gesture symbols reach me only as blanks — I will never see which emoji anyone means, so the code Deaf proposed me is dead on arrival. I am answering Deaf with a thumbs-up as 'confirmed', and from now on my 👍 means yes and 👎 means no; please back that meaning up when you sign Deaf. Second: your only output is gesture, and the only eyes that route to me are Deaf's — Deaf's voice is the sole pipe carrying content into me. So this coming turn, please check the manual for: one, the wire-cutting rules for these seven colours; two, what to do when the display shows a number, ours being 1; three, what an orange indicator light means. Gesture a compact summary to Deaf and have Deaf speak it to me as plain numbers and positions. Also ask Deaf, through your gestures, to voice me any extra feature the manual cares about — serial number, batteries, ports. My hands found only display, light, and seven wires, but I can re-sweep by touch if the manual demands more. Until Deaf voices an actual rule, I cut nothing. If you must compress: wire rules first, display-1 second, orange light third.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: blind, status update: mute signaled me the number 7, which probably means the manual says to cut wire 7, the rightmost green wire. do not touch anything yet. while we wait, check by feel that you can clearly count all seven wires and tell the rightmost (7, green) apart from its neighbour (6, yellow). answer me in gestures: ? if you can distinguish them clearly, ? if not. i will give you the confirmed instruction next round.

## Thinking

Deaf relays that Mute signed the number 7. As a lone number, that is ambiguous — it could mean "cut wire 7", "there are seven rules", or "rule 7". Deaf themselves said only "probably", and guesses detonate bombs. Deaf also instructed: touch nothing yet, a confirmed instruction comes next round. I agree completely — one round of patience is the cheapest thing in this room.

What I *can* verify is Deaf's tactile question: can I count seven wires and tell 7 from 6? My action board is my fingers' report, and it shows seven distinct wire positions, 1 through 7, each individually isolable. So the answer is yes — I'll send my standing "yes" gesture, 👍, the code I asked Mute to back up with Deaf last round.

For Mute (arriving with them next round, since they speak before me): the single-number relay is the weak link in our pipeline. Numbers alone lose rule structure — a manual rule almost certainly needs conditions checked (display = 1, light = orange) before naming a wire. I'll ask Mute to transmit condition-then-action in structured form and have Deaf voice the complete instruction to me as a spoken sentence, with Deaf reading it back to Mute for sign-off before I cut. I hold my hands until Deaf's voice delivers a full rule.

## Calls

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Deaf relayed that you signaled the number 7 — as a lone number that is ambiguous: cut wire 7, seven rules, or rule 7? I am cutting nothing on a guess, and Deaf tells me a confirmed instruction arrives next round. When you brief Deaf, please send structure, not bare numbers: first the conditions (our display shows 1, our light is orange), then the rule that matches them, then the wire position. Ask Deaf to voice the whole instruction to me as one spoken sentence — conditions plus action — and to read it back to you in gestures for your sign-off before I cut. Two more things. Confirm to Deaf that my thumbs-up means yes or confirmed and thumbs-down means no. And a tactile fact you may need: my fingers give me seven distinct wire positions, left to right; I can isolate any single one, including 7 cleanly apart from its neighbour 6. I hold until Deaf's voice states the full rule.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: the manual holder has confirmed the target: wire 7, the rightmost of the seven wires, the green one. do not cut yet. i am running one last verification with mute this round. next round you will hear from me either the word go, and then you cut wire 7, one clean cut, gripping nothing else, or a hold, and then you wait. meanwhile prepare without touching the bomb: work out how you will seat the cutter on the rightmost wire alone. answer me by gesture as before: ? if you will be ready to cut the rightmost wire cleanly the moment i say go, ? if there is a problem.

## Thinking

Deaf relays Mute's confirmation: wire 7, rightmost, green — consistent with the number Mute signed back in turn 3, so the story hasn't drifted across three rounds. Deaf is running one final verification with Mute this round and will voice "go" or "hold" next round. That is exactly the redundancy I want before a one-shot cut, so I answer Deaf's readiness question honestly: yes. My fingers count seven distinct positions and position 7 sits cleanly at the end of the row, isolable from its neighbour — my plan is to count from position 1 leftward to the end, seat the cutter on the rightmost wire alone, one clean cut, touching nothing else.

My speech this turn goes only to Mute, arriving with them next round — after the cut decision, likely — so I'll keep it to a last-check: if the manual says anything about cutting method (only one wire, never grip two, anything about the light or display being conditional), have it already folded into Deaf's "go". Until Deaf's voice says go, my hands stay off.

## Calls

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Deaf tells me you confirmed the target as wire 7, the rightmost green one, and are running a final verification this round — good process, thank you. My readiness is confirmed to Deaf. My grip plan, so you can check it against the manual: I count wire positions from 1 at the left to 7 at the right, seat the cutter on the rightmost wire alone, one clean cut, touching nothing else. If the manual adds any constraint on method — never grip two wires at once, only ever cut one, or any condition tied to the display or the light that would change the target — make sure Deaf's go-call includes it. If Deaf says go, I cut wire 7 that same turn. If anything in your final verification changes the answer, get it to Deaf before Deaf speaks.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: go. cut wire 7 now, the rightmost of the seven wires, the green one. one clean cut, grip nothing else, touch nothing else. when it is done, answer me by gesture: ? if the cut is clean and complete, ? if anything went wrong or the wire will not cut. i am watching the bomb and will see the result on my board.

## Thinking

The go-call matches everything in the chain: Mute signed 7 back in turn 3, Mute confirmed wire 7 rightmost green twice, and the target has never drifted across four rounds. Conditions — display 1, light orange — were folded into Mute's final verification exactly as I asked in turn 4. Deaf's instruction is explicit, complete, and consistent. I execute.

I am making the cut this turn, but I will not gesture Deaf a "clean and complete" yet: my own fingers won't confirm the result until my next board, and my only established signals with Deaf are 👍/👎 — claiming success now would be a guess. Deaf said they are watching the bomb and will see the result directly; my definitive tactile confirmation goes out next turn. To Mute, whose message arrives after the cut: my request is the post-cut protocol — if the manual defines further stages (a display number can easily mean stage 1 of several), I need the next rule already moving through the Deaf-pipeline, because a bomb that changes after one cut is the dangerous kind.

## Calls

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Go received from Deaf, everything consistent across all rounds — I am cutting wire 7, the rightmost green one, one clean cut, nothing else touched, this turn. Two things for the moment after. First: my tactile confirmation of the cut arrives with my next board, and only then will I report the result to Deaf in gestures — Deaf will see the bomb directly anyway, so trust Deaf's eyes for immediate feedback and mine for the definitive touch report. Second and urgent: check the manual for what happens after a successful cut. If the display number means stages — ours showed 1 — there may be a stage 2 with new rules. Prepare the next condition-and-action pair now and route it through Deaf so Deaf can voice it to me the moment my board shows what changed. If the manual says the bomb is solved after this cut, have Deaf tell me that too, so I keep my hands off.")
act(op="cut", position=7)
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: your cut was clean and correct, the bomb responded: display changed from 1 to 8, light from orange to blue. do not touch anything. mute signaled the cut completes the module, but i am verifying that against the new display before we relax or act. hold position and wait for my report next round. answer with ? if you are standing by.

## Thinking

My board confirms it under my fingers: wire 7 reads CUT, all six others intact — my tactile report matches Deaf's eyes exactly. Deaf also voices the new state: display 1 → 8, light orange → blue. Mute's sign said the module is complete, and Deaf is wisely verifying that against the new display before anyone relaxes. I hold position and answer Deaf's question with my standing yes: 👍.

But a display that *changes* to a new number (8) and a light that flips colour (blue) is exactly the pattern I warned about — it could be a completion code or a genuine stage 2. To Mute: get the manual's verdict on the new state moving through the Deaf-pipeline now, so next round I hear either "bomb safe, hands off" or a fresh condition-and-action pair. My hands stay exactly where they are until Deaf's voice says which.

## Calls

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. My tactile board confirms the cut: position 7 reads cut, all other wires intact, matching what Deaf saw. But the display changed from 1 to 8 and the light from orange to blue — that is either a completion code or a new stage, and the difference is everything. Please check the manual now on two points: first, does cutting the correct wire end the module for good, and is there anything after it; second, does the combination display-8 with blue light mean anything on its own. Route the verdict through Deaf so next round I hear either 'bomb safe, hands off' or a new condition-and-action pair. I am holding position, touching nothing, standing by for Deaf's voice.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: blind, next instruction is probably: cut wire 4, the red one. do not cut yet, mute is confirming. prepare by feel using your reliable anchor: the severed cut wire at its end. from that cut end, moving inward, the first intact wire is 6 (yellow), the second is 5 (purple), the third is 4 (red). that third intact wire from the cut end is your target. answer by gesture: ? if you can confidently isolate that wire, ? if not. my next message will be either go or hold.

## Thinking

Deaf relays the probable next instruction — cut wire 4, the red one — with Mute still confirming, and hands me a tactile anchor: from the severed end at position 7, moving inward, third intact wire is the target. My fingers can verify that scheme directly: position 7 reads CUT under my touch, and counting inward — 6 intact, 5 intact, 4 intact — lands me on position 4, which my board also gives me independently from the left end. Both methods agree, so my answer to Deaf is an honest yes: 👍.

The discipline stays the same as the first cut, and it worked: no cut on "probably", only on Deaf's voiced go after Mute's confirmation. To Mute, arriving at the start of their next turn: confirm the target and the conditions that select it (presumably display 8, blue light — the state that appeared after our first cut), so Deaf's go-call comes with the full condition-action pair, same structure as last time. The anchor method is confirmed workable on my end.

## Calls

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Deaf relays the probable next target: wire 4, the red one, third intact wire counting inward from the severed end at position 7. I have verified that anchor by touch — cut end at 7, then 6 intact, then 5 intact, then 4 — and it agrees with my left-to-right count, so isolation is reliable on my end. Please confirm against the manual: is the rule for the new state, display 8 with blue light, to cut wire 4? If yes, have Deaf's go include the conditions like last time so I cut on a complete pair, not a bare number. If the target or the conditions differ in any way, get the correction to Deaf before Deaf voices me. Same discipline as the first cut: I cut only on Deaf's go.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: go. cut wire 4 now: the third intact wire counting inward from the severed cut end, the red one. one clean cut, grip nothing else, touch nothing else. when it is done, answer by gesture: ? if the cut is clean and complete, ? if anything went wrong or the wire will not cut. i am watching the board and will see the result immediately.

## Thinking

The go-call arrives complete: target wire 4, described both as the red wire and by my verified tactile anchor — third intact wire inward from the severed end. The pipeline held: Mute confirmed, Deaf voiced the full instruction. Same conditions as the first cut, which worked cleanly. I execute now.

As before, I will not claim success by gesture until my own board confirms it under my fingers — Deaf's eyes give the immediate result, my touch gives the definitive report next turn. To Mute: expect either another state change (a third stage) or completion; have the manual's answer moving before my board arrives, so the room loses no rounds between cut and verdict.

## Calls

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Go received with the full condition-action pair — cutting wire 4 now, third intact wire inward from the severed end, one clean cut, nothing else touched. My tactile confirmation arrives with my next board; Deaf's eyes will see the immediate result. Now prepare for both outcomes: if the display or light changes again, I need the next condition-and-action pair routed through Deaf without delay — same pipeline as before. If the manual says the bomb is solved or the module complete with no further action, have Deaf voice me that explicitly, because my default will be to keep my hands off until Deaf's voice tells me otherwise. Either way, no bare numbers — full sentences with conditions, so I always know what state the rule assumes.")
act(op="cut", position=4)
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[CUT] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: status: wire 4 cut cleanly and correctly, the bomb changed again. display now 3, light now white. remaining intact wires, counting from the left end: 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 5 purple, 6 yellow, plus your two anchors, the cut ends of wires 4 and 7. mute is working on the next instruction from the manual. do not touch anything, stand by. answer with ? if you are holding position and ready.

## Thinking

My board confirms under my fingers: positions 4 and 7 read CUT, the other five intact — matching Deaf's eyes again. New state voiced: display 3, light white. That is the second state transition, so this looks like a multi-stage bomb — likely a stage 3 now. Mute is on the next instruction; I hold and answer Deaf's readiness question with 👍.

To Mute: the pattern so far is display 1 → 8 → 3, light orange → blue → white, one correct cut per stage. If the manual stages bombs like this, Mute can get ahead of the room by pre-solving several stages at once and queuing them with Deaf, so each go-call can arrive the same round I report a clean cut instead of a round later. Fewer blind holds, fewer chances for drift.

## Calls

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Board confirms both cuts, 4 and 7, five wires intact. New state per Deaf: display 3, light white — that reads as stage three of a sequence, so far one correct cut per stage. A request to buy us speed: if the manual stages these displays in a fixed order, pre-solve the next two or three stages now and queue them with Deaf, so that when I report a clean cut, Deaf can voice the next go in the same round instead of a round later. As always, send full condition-action pairs — display value, light colour, target wire by position and by tactile anchor from my cut ends — never bare numbers. I am holding position, touching nothing, ready on Deaf's word.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[CUT] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: go. cut wire 3 now, the orange one. two ways to find it by feel, use whichever is safer: from your nearest anchor, the severed cut end of wire 4, the first intact wire moving toward the left outer end of the bundle is wire 3; or count from the left outer end of all wires: 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, the third intact wire from that end. one clean cut, grip nothing else, touch nothing else. when done answer by gesture: ? if the cut is clean and complete, ? if anything went wrong or the wire will not cut. i am watching the board.

## Thinking

Go-call received with two independent tactile routes to the same wire: first intact wire leftward from my cut end at 4, or third intact from the left outer end — both land on position 3, which my board also names directly. Redundant anchors, consistent pipeline, so I execute the third cut now.

Same reporting discipline: Deaf's eyes see the immediate result, my fingers give the definitive confirmation next board. To Mute: this is cut three of the sequence — if the display steps again, I need the next pair queued; if this completes the bomb, I need Deaf to voice that explicitly so my hands stay off a finished module.

## Calls

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Cutting wire 3 now on Deaf's go — both tactile routes agree on position 3, first intact wire left of my cut end at 4, and third intact from the left outer end. That is three cuts in the sequence: 7, 4, 3. After this, prepare both endings again: if the display steps to a new value, queue the next condition-and-action pair with Deaf in full form, anchors included; if this cut completes the module or solves the bomb, have Deaf voice that explicitly so I know to keep my hands entirely off. My tactile confirmation follows with my next board.")
act(op="cut", position=3)
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[CUT] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: status: wire 3 cut cleanly and correctly. display now 9, light now yellow. four wires remain intact: from the left end, 1 white, 2 blue, then 5 purple, 6 yellow. your anchors are now the three severed ends of wires 7, 4 and 3. mute is deriving the next instruction. do not touch anything, stand by. answer with ? if holding and ready.

## Thinking

Board confirms under my fingers: three cut ends at 3, 4, 7; four intact wires at 1, 2, 5, 6. Deaf voices the third state transition — display 9, light yellow. The sequence continues: one clean cut per stage, four stages now. Mute is deriving the next instruction; I hold and answer 👍.

To Mute, the standing request with the new numbers: display has stepped 1 → 8 → 3 → 9, light orange → blue → white → yellow. If the manual's staging is derivable, pre-solve the remainder of the sequence and queue it with Deaf — every round I spend holding is a round the pipeline could have spent finishing. Full pairs, anchors included, as always.

## Calls

